Hi Nikhil —

Thanks for the runbook you shared in the call. We reviewed at FinX and have a few constraints to confirm before we schedule a maintenance window:

- We require a pinned version policy: we cannot accept a rolling major version bump. Any upgrade must allow us to pin the model and runtime for 14 days after the rollout.
- Network gating: our ops team needs a maintenance-cidr-based preflight that ensures control-plane access for audit logs during the window.
- Rollback SLAs: we need a documented rollback ladder with timed checkpoints and an emergency snapshot restore option.

Can your team confirm those items are included in the runbook attachments you promised? Also, prefer a weekday late-evening window (US-PDT) to minimize business impact.

Harriet

Harriet —

Thanks for the quick read. Confirming everything you asked is covered; attaching the preflight checklist and the detailed rollback-runbook for your ops and compliance teams. High level on each ask: 

1) Version pinning: our Private control plane supports "pin sets". The runbook describes creating a pin for the customer model + runtime package (OS-level package and runtimeSHA) and an enforcement window of 14 days. We include a TTL and an automated alert that fires 48 hours before pin expiry.

2) Network gating: the preflight workbook has the CIDR gating steps — we ask you to provision a maintenance CIDR and a short-lived control-plane tunnel credential. The checklist also validates that audit-collection sinks (S3/GCS or your SIEM endpoint) are reachable during the window.

3) Rollback ladder: attached PDF enumerates a 4-step ladder: 1) soft revert (config toggles & scaled canary rollback), 2) canary redeploy to prior pin, 3) cluster slice revert + traffic shift (30/70 -> 0/100 within 20m), 4) snapshot restore (last-known-good) and full evacuation. Each step includes abort criteria and owner.

Proposed window: Wed Aug 19, 22:00-01:00 PDT (3 hours). We will run a 5% canary for the first 20 minutes, then 25%, then full cutover if health signals are green. If you want a longer verification period we can extend the canary.

Next steps: please confirm the window and share the maintenance CIDR and the contact for your on-call netops. I will schedule a prep dry-run two days prior.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Customer Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Looping in a couple of operational details from the operator runbook that FinX may want to tweak: 

- Canary cadence: we typically do 5% for 10–15 minutes, not 20, to reduce blast radius. The doc allows you to override. If FinX requires longer verifications for compliance, flag it and we will mark that in the audit trail.
- KV cache drains: for on-prem model-serving, we recommend a per-pod KV eviction with a 2-minute overlap to avoid cold-start token overhead. The runbook lists the commands and an idempotent drain script (ops/drain-kv.sh).
- Metrics: we will instrument token-latency p95, success-rate, and user-facing error-rate. The rollback ladder uses thresholds: p95 increase >25% OR user error-rate >0.5% sustained for 3 consecutive minutes triggers immediate step-1 rollback.
- Control-plane access: we can generate a time-limited control-plane key that is rotatable and logged to your SIEM.

I'll be operator-on-call for the dry-run on Aug 17. Ben, can you confirm that the dedicated pool scaling and snapshot retention (48h) are ready for FinX?

Marissa
Sr. Ops Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
